author: Lisa Balick
title: Tigard Mayor vows to improve leadership culture after back-to-back resignations - NewsBreak
text:
By Lisa Balick Danny Peterson ,
4 hours ago
PORTLAND, Ore. ( KOIN ) — Following Tigard City Manager Brent Stockwell ‘s resignation after less than six months on the job, the mayor is addressing the sudden shakeup.
KOIN 6 News asked Mayor Yi-Kang Hu if he could confirm reports that Stockwell’s resignation on Nov. 18 came while he was on leave, as reported by OPB .
In response, Mayor Hu said he couldn’t go into whether or not the city placed Stockwell on leave since it is a personnel decision.
OR National Guard to demobilize: ‘Finally heading home’ Brent Stockwell resigned as Tigard City manager on Nov. 18, 2025 after taking on the role in June (Courtesy City of Tigard). “But I can say that we had a discussion about city leadership and direction. And after that discussion, Mr. Stockwell, voluntarily, chose to resign,” Mayor Hu told KOIN 6 News. “Anything beyond that will be personnel matters.”
According to the city, Acting City Manager Emily Tritsch will continue to serve in the interim. Following the resignation, the Tigard City Council is beginning the process of finding a long-term replacement.
The resignation comes after Stockwell took over as city manager on June 2 after serving as assistant city manager in Scottsdale, Arizona.
Stockwell’s resignation comes three months after another leadership shakeup in the city.
In September, Tigard Mayor Heidi Lueb announced her resignation , citing troubles within City Hall and power struggles occurring among the leadership.
In an independent investigation made public, Lueb was accused of workplace conduct violations.
According to the investigation, which was finalized one week before her abrupt resignation on Sept. 9, witnesses claimed Mayor Lueb engaged in bullying and yelled at councilors and staff, creating a hostile work environment .
PacifiCorp settles Labor Day fires suit: What to know KOIN 6 asked Mayor Hu what the city might be doing differently moving forward compared to how it’s been operating leading up to the recent shakeups.
Mayor Hu said that after former Mayor Lueb resigned, “the city council made a public commitment to do everything better, you know, with our leadership, with our communication, and with accountability within our organization.”
“So the council, you know, has not changed our commitment,” Mayor Hu continued. “So this leadership change is part of moving forward with our city that’s more transparent, has a more respectful and healthy work environment and provide more transparency for our community members.”
Heidi Lueb as seen on her website on Sept. 10, 2025 (KOIN) When asked how he plans to prevent further resignations from continuing, Mayor Hu said the city council’s commitment to change includes training “regarding culture and how we treat each other.”
The training for senior city leadership will begin in December, and for councilors it will begin in late January, Hu said.
Oregon bans bump stocks, limits guns in public spaces “The acting city manager right now is holding more office hours…I’m committed to being more out in the community,” Mayor Hu said, adding he aims to rebuild trust in the community by having more face-to-face interactions with citizens.
Hu acknowledged there needs to be a culture change within city leadership circles “to be more supportive, and more respectful and more transparent with our community and with city staff.”
He added that city councilors are behind the idea of providing more support for city staff to ensure “they have a respectful and supportive working environment.”
“They work so hard behind the scenes 24/7 to provide excellent service,” Hu said.
The first of Mayor Hu’s planned monthly “ Meet Up with the Mayor ” events with the public is on Thursday evening from 5:30 p.m. to 6:30 p.m. at Flyboy Brewery and Pub in Tigard.
